lyrics:
[Intro: bright banjo and mandolin figure]

[Verse 1: warm male voice, storytelling]
I was seventeen, gravel in my shoes
Standing in her yard with nothing to lose
Her daddy on the steps with his arms crossed tight
Said, "Son, I don't think so. Not tonight."

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
I threw rocks at her window, I learned to climb
I wore that old man down one Sunday at a time

[Chorus: full band, soaring]
And she said yes, on a dirt road, in the rain
And her daddy shook my hand and he called me by my name
I swore I'd never be the man on that porch
Funny how the story goes
Now I'm the one at the door

[Verse 2: voice lower, amused]
There's a truck in my drive with a muffler like a drum
A boy in a clean shirt, chewing on his thumb
And my little girl's upstairs, taking her time
And every word her granddad said is lining up in mine

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
I got my arms crossed tight, I got the look down cold
Then I see my own knees shaking, seventeen years old

[Chorus: full band, soaring]
'Cause she said yes, on a dirt road, in the rain
And her daddy shook my hand and he called me by my name
I swore I'd never be the man on that porch
Funny how the story goes
Now I'm the one at the door

[Bridge: band drops to banjo, tender]
So I walk down the steps and I look him in the eye
I say, "Have her home by ten."
He says, "Yes, sir." I say, "Nine."

[Final Chorus: key change up, full band and strings]
And someday she'll say yes, on some road, in some rain
And I'll shake that boy's hand and I'll call him by his name
I swore I'd never be the man on that porch
Lord, I love how the story goes
Now I'm the one at the door

[Outro: banjo figure, a truck pulling away, spoken]
Nine-thirty's fine.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 119 BPM, 4/4, D major, rising to E major for the last chorus. Bright and galloping, a story told at a run.

VOICE: Male tenor, warm and clear, telling a story with a smile in it. Fuller and higher in the choruses. Spoken lines in the bridge and at the end, played for gentle comedy.

INSTRUMENTS: Banjo and mandolin playing a repeating figure, strummed acoustic guitar, fiddle, bright electric guitar, bass, driving live drums, a string section in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro figure. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:34 Pre-chorus. 0:44 Chorus 1. 1:10 Verse 2. 1:34 Pre-chorus. 1:44 Chorus 2. 2:10 Bridge, banjo only. 2:30 Final chorus, key up, strings. 3:02 Outro, a truck pulling away, the spoken line at 3:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2008 pop-country: shiny, wide, acoustic instruments bright on top of a pop rhythm section.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The key change at 2:30, landing on 'someday she'll say yes'.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is the girl on the balcony. Thirty years later the boy from that story is the father in the way, and he finds he is glad to be.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Remembering, bristling, recognising himself, giving way.
